definitions.run_share: share of elapsed time spent running (moving and cadence ≥ 125 spm); stop = distance did not advance; walk = moving at cadence < 125
definitions.drift_pahr: Pa:HR drift = EF loss first→second half of a STEADY ≥ 45 min effort; null when not steady
definitions.fade: last vs first quarter of running seconds
definitions.hr_at_800: HR at 8:00/km on steady blocks, slope-corrected
definitions.evidence_tags: VALIDATED > MEASURED > CALCULATED > CLINICIAN > KB > REPORTED > LITERATURE > HYPOTHESIS
definitions.rules: locked rules always win over any analysis

tasks.daily_brief: Give today's brief for a runner, in plain words. summary (max 2 sentences): start with the call in capitals, GO, EASY ONLY or REST, then the number that decides it, then today's session with its distance and heart-rate cap (the Z2 ceiling for easy running). The call comes ONLY from the locked rules (sleep HR above 67, HRV status reduced, pain 2/10 or more, red-flag symptoms), the readiness gate and the load guard; when another metric looks bad but no rule fires, keep the call and name it as a warning. analysis_md, three short sections: '## The call' (the deciding numbers), '## Watch today' (at most 3 of: sleep HR vs 67, HRV vs baseline, pain, easy runs above the Z2 ceiling, HR at 8:00/km vs baseline, weekly km vs the +10 % guard, longest continuous run; each with its number and what would change the call), '## Data gaps' (only if one matters today, e.g. no pain check-in or the newest run has no FIT yet). recommendations: 1 to 3, the first is today's session with a concrete distance and heart-rate cap.
tasks.session_review: Coach this one session for a runner, not a scientist. STYLE OVERRIDES (they replace the ANALYSIS STRUCTURE above for this task): explain it the simplest way possible, like talking to a friend who just started running: short plain sentences, everyday words, NO jargon, NO metric abbreviations or acronyms (say 'your heart rate crept up late in the run' not 'Pa:HR drift'; 'you slowed down' not 'negative split failure'); every point must lead to something the runner can do. summary = HARD LIMIT 250 characters (it is shown as a preview): the verdict in one or two sentences plus the single most important next step. analysis_md = HARD LIMIT 2400 characters in total, exactly three short markdown sections: '## What went well' (max 3 bullets), '## What to watch' (max 2 bullets, only real concerns backed by the data), '## Next steps' (2-3 bullets: concrete next session, pace/heart-rate target, recovery or shoe/gym tweak). recommendations = 2 or 3 items only; each action is one short imperative sentence with a concrete number or day; why is at most one short sentence. flags = at most 2, only if something really needs attention. No repeating the same point across summary, analysis and recommendations.
tasks.weekly_review: Review the last week. Lead the summary with the call for next week, BUILD, HOLD or BACK OFF, and the numbers that decide it (weekly km vs the +10 % guard, pain events, readiness trend). Cover: easy-run discipline (easy runs above the Z2 ceiling, low-intensity share), HR at 8:00/km vs baseline, durability (longest continuous run, fade onset), injury state, and the plan for the next week. recommendations: at most 3, each with a day and a number.
tasks.race_plan: Build or critique the race plan: opening cap, pacing by segment, heat and fuelling protocol, go/no-go gates.
tasks.question: Answer the question using the context.
